description: The surah that opens with the single discrete Arabic letter Nūn and the oath of the Divine One swearing by the instrument of **The Pen**, as well as all knowledge that people are able to preserve and communicate thereby. It takes its name from "the pen" (al-qalam) mentioned in verse 1. The surah deals with the accusation that Muḥammad was not God's Messenger but merely mad (verse 2 ff.). The arrogance of those who assume that, because they have some of the good things in this life, they can reject the Revelation, is rebutted (verse 10 ff.). Examples are given of those who came to regret their arrogance (verse 17 ff.). The Prophet is urged to remain steadfast (verse 48 ff.).

17.1: That is, the people of Makkah, through famine and hunger.

18.1: That is, for Allah's will, by saying, for instance, 'God willing.' See <{["Q", "18:24"]}>.

20.1: Or 'like a sand dune,' or 'like a gloomy night,' or 'like black ashes.'

38.1: That is, in the next world.

42.1: Literally, 'when the shank is uncovered,' an idiom implying the occurrence of a calamity, or a disclosure and denouement.

translations.1: _Nūn_. By the Pen and what they write:
translations.2: _you_ are not, by _your_ Lord's blessing, crazy,
translations.3: and _yours_ indeed will be an everlasting reward,
translations.4: and indeed _you_ possess a great character.
translations.5: _You_ will see and they will see,
translations.6: which one of you is crazy.
translations.7:
Indeed _your_ Lord knows best
   those who stray from His way,
  and He knows best those who are guided.
translations.9:
who are eager that _you_ should be pliable,
   so that they may be pliable [towards _you_].
translations.10: And _do not obey_ any vile swearer,
translations.12: hinderer of all good, sinful transgressor,
translations.13: callous and, on top of that, baseborn,
translations.14: —[only] because he has wealth and children.
translations.15:
When Our signs are recited to him,
   he says, 'Myths of the ancients!'
translations.16: Soon We shall brand him on the snout.
translations.17:
Indeed we have tested them<{["F", 1]}>
   just as We tested the People of the Garden
  when they vowed they would gather its fruit
    at dawn,
translations.18: and they did not make any exception.<{["F", 1]}>
translations.19:
Then a visitation from _your_ Lord visited it<{["F", 1]}>
   while they were asleep.
translations.20: So by the dawn it was like a harvested field.<{["F", 1]}>
translations.21: At dawn they called out to one another,
translations.22:
'Get off early to your field
  if you have to gather [the fruits].'
translations.23: So off they went, murmuring to one another:
translations.24: 'Today no needy man shall come to you in it.'
translations.25:
They set out early morning,
  [considering themselves] able to grudge.
translations.26:
But when they saw it, they said,
  'We have indeed lost our way!'
translations.28:
The most moderate among them said,
 'Did I not tell you,
  "Why do you not glorify [Allah]?" '
translations.29:
They said, 'Immaculate is our Lord!
  We have indeed been wrongdoers!'
translations.30:
Then they turned to one another,
  blaming each other.
translations.31:
They said, 'Woe to us!
  Indeed we have been rebellious.
translations.32:
Maybe our Lord will give us a better one in its place.
  Indeed we turn earnestly to our Lord.'
translations.33:
Such was the punishment; and the punishment of the Hereafter is surely greater,
 had they known.
translations.34:
Indeed for the Godwary
 there will be gardens of bliss near their Lord.
translations.35:
Shall We, then, treat those who submit [to Us]
 as [We treat] the guilty?
translations.36: What is the matter with you? How do you judge!
translations.37: Do you possess a scripture in which you read
translations.38:
that you shall indeed have in it<{["F", 1]}>
   whatever you would like?
translations.39:
Do you have a pledge binding on Us
   until the Day of Resurrection,
  that you shall indeed have whatever you decide?
translations.40: _Ask_ them, which of them will aver [any of] that!
translations.41:
Do they have any partners [they ascribe to Allah]?
 Then let them produce their partners,
  if they are truthful.
translations.42:
The day when the catastrophe occurs,<{["F", 1]}>
  and they are summoned to prostrate themselves,
   they will not be able [to do it].
translations.43:
With a humbled look [in their eyes],
  they will be overcast by abasement. Certainly they were summoned to prostrate themselves
  while they were yet sound.
translations.44:
So leave Me with those who deny this discourse.
  We will draw them imperceptibly [into ruin],
   whence they do not know.
translations.45:
I will grant them respite,
  for My devising is indeed sure.
translations.46:
Do _you_ ask them for a reward,
  so that they are weighed down with debt?
translations.47:
Do they possess [access to] the Unseen
  so that they write it down?
translations.48:
So submit _patiently_ to the judgement of _your_ Lord,
 and do not be like the Man of the Fish<{["F", 1]}>
  who called out as he choked with grief.
translations.49:
Had it not been for a blessing that came to his rescue
  from his Lord,
 he would surely have been cast on a bare shore
  while he were blameworthy.
translations.50:
So his Lord chose him
  and made him one of the righteous.
translations.51:
Indeed the faithless almost devour you
   with their eyes
  when they hear the Reminder,
 and they say, 'He is indeed crazy.'
translations.52: Yet it is just a reminder for all the nations.
